jobs.title: Senior Planning Officer (Career Grade)
jobs.description:
**Help shape the future of one of the country’s most varied boroughs**
======================================================================


From historic city streets and major regeneration sites to thriving towns, rural communities and protected countryside, planning in Cheshire West and Chester is rarely ordinary.


We’re looking for a motivated and experienced planner to join our friendly and supportive Development Management team. You’ll take ownership of a varied caseload, apply your professional judgement to interesting and challenging proposals, and have the autonomy to make decisions that deliver positive outcomes for communities across the borough.


Organisation
Cheshire West and Chester Council
Location
Ellesmere Port
Job Category
Environmental and Public Services
Grade
Please refer to advert text

£39,481 per annum
Salary Max
£49,658 per annum

37

Ref No
W4830
Documents  
Cheshire West and Chester Council is a place where everyone can Thrive – through our core values of Teamwork, Honesty, Respect, Innovation, Value for Money and Empowerment.


**The opportunity**
===================


Whether you're an experienced Planner ready for progression or an established Senior Planner looking for your next opportunity, we'd love to hear from you. This career grade post spans Grades 9 and 10, with the starting grade and salary reflecting your qualifications, experience and professional expertise.
Our borough brings together the historic city of Chester, the towns of Ellesmere Port, Northwich and Winsford, and extensive rural areas, countryside and Green Belt. With around 3,000 planning applications handled each year, no two days \- or cases \-are quite the same.


Your work could include:


* Major housing developments
* Significant commercial, industrial and energy proposals, including development associated with the Origin industrial area
* Agricultural and rural diversification schemes
* Leading visitor destinations such as Chester Zoo, Oulton Park and Chester Racecourse
* Proposals affecting our many conservation areas and listed buildings, and Chester’s Area of Archaeological Importance

It’s a chance to broaden your experience, tackle complex planning issues and see the real\-world impact of your work across the borough.


**What you’ll do**
------------------


You’ll manage and determine a varied caseload of complex planning applications, working with applicants, residents, colleagues and other stakeholders to secure high\-quality, sustainable development.


You may also have opportunities to support our planning enforcement and planning policy teams, giving you wider experience across the service.


**What you’ll bring**
---------------------


We’re looking for someone who:


* Has experience of dealing with varied and complex planning issues, preferably within a local authority
* Communicates clearly and builds effective working relationships
* Can balance competing priorities and take ownership of decisions
* Uses sound professional judgement to find practical solutions
* Is committed to providing great service to applicants, residents and communities

**How we work**


We work as a large, friendly and supportive team, built on trust, autonomy and open communication. We share knowledge, offer different perspectives and tackle challenges together. Managers give you the space to use your professional judgement, while making sure support is there when you need it.


This is a hybrid role, with your time split between home and our modern offices in Ellesmere Port. We support flexible working and a healthy work\-life balance.


Part\-time working arrangements may be considered where the proposed pattern meets the operational needs of the service. If you’re looking to balance the role with family or other commitments, contact us to discuss what could work.


The role involves site visits and remote meetings, so you’ll need a full UK driving licence and access to a car.


**Interested?**
---------------


For an informal conversation about the role, contact:


Nick Smith, Planning Team Manager Nick.Smith2@cheshirewestandchester.gov.uk


To learn more about working for Cheshire West and Chester Council, including our rewards and benefits, visit http://www.cwcrecruitment.co.uk.


For technical enquiries, email Sourcingteam@ecwip.co.uk and quote the job reference number in all correspondence.


Cheshire West and Chester Council is committed to equality and diversity in employment.

jobs.title: Urban Planner
jobs.description:
**JOB SUMMARY**
The Urban Planner I or II position performs advanced professional and administrative work in the field of urban planning under the general supervision of the Director of Planning. The position is responsible for coordinating and managing a variety of current and long\-range planning activities, including development review, zoning administration, comprehensive planning initiatives, research, and project coordination.  

  

The Urban Planner I or II exercises independent judgment in the interpretation and application of planning principles, zoning regulations, subdivision regulations, and related ordinances. The position serves as a primary point of contact for developers, property owners, consultants, public officials, and citizens regarding planning and development matters and provides technical guidance throughout the development review process.  

  

Work requires a high degree of customer service, analytical ability, professionalism, and effective communication while coordinating with multiple agencies, departments, boards, commissions, and the public to support the orderly growth and development of the Town of Elkton.  

  

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**
* Coordinates and prepares planning studies, reports, recommendations, and related research involving land use, zoning, redevelopment, transportation, housing, sustainability, and community development initiatives.
* Participates in and coordinates updates to the Comprehensive Plan, zoning ordinance, subdivision regulations, maps, and related planning documents, including drafting ordinance amendments and staff reports.
* Conducts technical review of subdivision plans, site plans, re\-zonings, annexations, special exception applications, variances, and related development proposals for compliance with applicable Town ordinances, policies, regulations, and planning objectives.
* Serves as project manager for assigned development applications and planning initiatives, including coordination with developers, consultants, engineers, reviewing agencies, and Town staff.
* Interprets and explains zoning regulations, subdivision requirements, development procedures, and planning policies to the public, applicants, developers, consultants, and Town officials.
* Provides professional staff support to the Elkton Planning Commission, Historic District Commission, Board of Appeals, and other boards or committees as assigned, including preparation of agendas, staff reports, presentations, public hearing materials, correspondence, minutes, and maintenance of official files.
* Coordinates project reviews and facilitates interagency review processes with local, county, state, and regional agencies.
* Conducts research, collects and analyzes data, prepares surveys, and develops maps, graphs, tables, and other illustrative materials to support planning projects and reports.
* Conducts field investigations and site inspections related to development applications, zoning compliance, and planning studies.
* Researches and responds to complex citizen inquiries, development concerns, and zoning\-related issues utilizing sound professional judgment, customer service skills, and conflict resolution techniques.
* Communicates effectively, both orally and in writing, with professionals and non\-professionals regarding planning, zoning, and development matters.
* Represents the Planning Department at interdepartmental meetings, regional committees, public meetings, trainings, seminars, and professional conferences as assigned.
* Maintains accurate records, files, and documentation related to planning and zoning activities.
* Takes initiative in completing assigned and unassigned tasks in support of the Planning Department and Town operations.
* Ability to prepare, administer, and monitor departmental budgets and grants.
* Works Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with regular mandatory evening meetings as well as occasional trainings and seminars outside normal business hours. Maintains good attendance record.

**ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES**
* Assists other Town departments with planning\-related matters as necessary.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES**
* Thorough knowledge of the principles, practices, methods, and objectives of municipal and regional planning.
* Knowledge of zoning administration, subdivision regulations, land development review processes, and comprehensive planning practices.
* Knowledge of Maryland land use law and municipal planning practices preferred.
* Ability to interpret and apply zoning ordinances, subdivision regulations, codes, policies, maps, aerial photography, engineering plans, and technical reports.
* Ability to analyze complex site plans, development applications, planning data, and technical information.
* Ability to prepare detailed staff reports, planning analyses, ordinances, correspondence, presentations, and professional recommendations.
* Ability to present technical information clearly and effectively before boards, commissions, elected officials, developers, consultants, and the public.
* Knowledge of general office practices, procedures, and standard office equipment.
* Proficiency in computer software programs including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and related planning software applications. GIS experience preferred.
* Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing.
* Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with coworkers, public officials, developers, consultants, property owners, and the general public.
* Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
* Ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously with minimal supervision.
* Must possess exceptional customer service skills and strong attention to detail.
* Ability to operate a Town vehicle.
* Ability to pass physical examinations, drug screenings, and background investigations.

**Help Us Make a Difference** 

We are currently seeking a Lead Urban Planner to join our team in Boston, Massachusetts.

This is a full\-time, 40\-hour per week position with a hybrid work schedule that allows for remote work on Mondays and Fridays.

The Lead Urban Planner is responsible for providing senior\-level technical leadership to project teams and delivering technically sound urban planning solutions that advance the organization’s project portfolio.

This role is a senior\-level technical contributor with project management responsibilities.

**About the Firm**

Planning and design professionals have spent decades talking about the problems with sprawl, but the needle has not moved. Inspire Placemaking Collective, Inc. was founded in 2022, to do something different. Instead of chasing contracts, we partner with cities and counties to drive results.

We are a mission\-driven firm that specializes in planning, landscape architecture, and graphic design. We partner with local governments to create great places, safe streets, and thriving communities and deliver high\-impact projects that put people and communities first.

**What You Will Do**

***Senior\-Level Technical Contributor Responsibilities***

· Provide senior\-level technical direction across multi\-disciplinary projects that require urban planning expertise. Conduct senior\-level technical reviews of project deliverables to ensure accuracy and quality.

· Evaluate complex comprehensive plans and land development regulations and recommend revisions or amendments needed to address statutory non\-compliance and inconsistencies between adopted policies and regulations.

· Synthesize qualitative and quantitative data from Census, market research, community engagement, and other sources. Conduct complex analyses to evaluate existing conditions and assess community trends and priorities to help shape project strategies.

· Develop maps with GIS software to evaluate spatial relationships and geographic patterns and recommend effective land use and development planning approaches.

· Revise policy and regulatory language to resolve inconsistencies between comprehensive plans and land development regulations. Draft proposed policy or regulatory amendments.

· Develop presentations, activities, and other materials and content for client and stakeholder meetings, community engagement events, public workshops, and charrettes. Incorporate client feedback or public input into recommendations and project deliverables.

· Develop reports, presentations, maps, and other technical documentation for project deliverables.

· Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams across the organization to ensure project objectives are achieved on schedule.

· Perform additional duties, as assigned.

***Project Management Responsibilities***

· Lead all phases of projects from planning to delivery, including scope, schedule, budget, staffing and resource allocation, technical production, and quality management.

Coordinate with the Principal\-in\-Charge, as needed.

· Actively monitor project performance against established project plans, including scopes, schedules, budgets, deliverables, and other Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to ensure project objectives are met and remain on target.

· Oversee the technical production and quality of projects, including staffing allocation and coordination and Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) reviews.

· Manage client relationships and expectations through ongoing communication related to project progress and status of deliverables. Address client feedback or other concerns that affect project scope, schedule, budget, technical production, quality, or overall client satisfaction.

· Identify business development opportunities and contribute to efforts to secure new or expanded work, such as participating in industry events or conferences.

· Provide clear direction to project team members related to project assignments, priorities, deadlines, and performance expectations.

· Perform additional duties, as assigned.

**Skills and Abilities** 

· Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams

· Proficiency in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) software, particularly ArcGIS

· Highly effective written and verbal communication skills

· Advanced analytical and critical thinking skills

· Proven ability to manage organizational priorities and complex workloads while consistently meeting deadlines

· Proven ability to work independently and effectively within team environments

**Minimum Requirements** 

· Education: Master's degree in Urban Planning, City Planning, Regional Planning, or a related field from an accredited Planning Accreditation Board (PAB) institution

· Years of experience: 10 years of relevant experience

· Professional Licenses, Registrations, or Certifications: Active AICP (American Institute of Certified Planners) Certification

**Preferred Qualifications**

· Prior project management experience

jobs.title: GIS Analyst
jobs.description:
ELOS Environmental, an Aventia Company (ELOS) maintains a competitive edge within the realm of environmental consulting by offering a diverse range of environmental services designed to satisfy our clients’ needs. We are proud of our record assisting clients with regulatory compliance issues. Members of our professional staff have extensive direct expertise with both the Federal and Louisiana wetland regulatory programs.

**Position Description:**


ELOS is seeking a GIS Analyst to assist a multidisciplinary team of accomplished GIS professionals and environmental scientists including biologists, ecologists, archaeologists, and project managers on a variety of projects. The GIS Analyst, under supervision from the GIS Manager, is responsible for processing and managing spatial and tabular data in a variety of formats (.gdb, .shp, .kmz, .dwg (AutoCAD), Trimble, field notes, etc.). The ideal candidate will work collaboratively with staff to create maps, exhibits, and figures to support technical reports.

**Essential Duties/Responsibilities (may include, but are not limited to):**

* Collect, organize, and maintain spatial and tabular environmental data (e.g., wetlands, wildlife habitats, soil types, land use, waterways, roadways, bridges, culverts).
* Perform spatial analysis to support environmental impact assessments, site selection, habitat modeling, risk analysis, and mitigation planning.
* Create high\-quality figures and graphics for technical reports, environmental permits, client presentations, and regulatory submittals.
* Ensure cartographic accuracy and adherence to project standards and symbology.
* Build and maintain geospatial databases for ongoing environmental monitoring or long\-term projects.
* Preparing figures for permit applications and compliance documents for agencies such as the USACE and state environmental agencies.
* Coordinate with field teams to collect geospatial data using GPS and mobile GIS tools (e.g., Collector for ArcGIS, Survey123\).
* Process and validate field data for integration into GIS projects.
* Work closely with environmental scientists, biologists, engineers, planners, and project managers to meet project goals.
* Translate technical environmental information into spatial data for stakeholder understanding.
* Use industry\-standard GIS software (e.g., ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online) and spatial analysis tools.
* Develop and maintain web maps, dashboards, or mobile data collection apps when required.
* Review spatial data for accuracy, completeness, and alignment with project specifications.

**Education:**

* Bachelor's degree in Geography, Environmental Science, GIS, or related field

**Experience/Desired Skills:**

* Minimum 2 years’ experience using ArcPro and ArcGIS Online
* Experience with ArcGIS Field Maps, Collector, Survey123, and StoryMaps.
* Proficient in performing spatial queries, overlays, and buffers.
* Strong understanding of coordinate systems, projections, and georeferencing.
* Skilled in integrating field\-collected GPS data and remote sensing datasets.
* Strong map design skills, including symbology, labeling, scale, and layout composition.
* Ability to create figures and graphics tailored for environmental reports, permitting documents, and public meetings.
* Basic to intermediate knowledge of Python for scripting and automation within ArcGIS (e.g., using ArcPy) preferred
* Experience supporting environmental impact assessments, ecological studies, remediation, or permitting is a plus.
* Experience using GNSS/GPS devices for data collection and QA/QC of spatial accuracy.
* Comfortable processing and integrating field data from mobile GIS apps.
* High level of accuracy in data handling, map production, and documentation.
* Experience working in multidisciplinary teams (e.g., biologists, engineers, planners).


Job Type: Full\-time


Benefits:

* Medical, Dental, \& Vision insurance
* 401(k) with matching
* Paid time off
* Life insurance


Schedule:

* Monday to Friday

* Coordinate with planning section on education and outreach. This includes developing training materials for applicants and grantees, attending workshops/conferences/open houses, and acting as backup on event scheduling and logistics.
* Represents the Florida Resilient staff in meetings with applicants, at public meetings, and at Department and interagency discussions related to projects and policy issues.
